successors.name: Republic of Florence
successors.text: Pisa and its countryside, 'annexation to the Republic of Florence' in 1406

ledger.x: c. 1000: the commune of Pisa. Infobox 'Established: c. 1000'; Henry IV 'granted them the right to name their own consuls, advised by a Council of Elders' (undated). The page says nothing of the state it left.
1051-1052: Pisa takes Corsica.
ledger.cp: Corsica (local rulers; no state named on the page)

ledger.x: June 1114: the Pisan-Catalan crusade reaches the Balearics.
1115: the Balearics are lost.
Cliopatria's shape drops three Corsican cells at the southern tip in 1202; neither the Corsica page nor the Pisa page mentions Bonifacio or any Genoese settlement.
1207: the Judicate of Cagliari under Pisan dominion.
1207: the Judicate of Gallura under Pisan dominion.
1256: Cagliari rebels against Pisa.
1258: Santa Igia falls.
1258: the Pisan dominion over Cagliari becomes possession.
1258: Pisa takes the Judicate of Cagliari, except what goes to Arborea and Gallura.
1282: the Corsican quarrel with Genoa.
1284: Corsica falls to Genoa.
5-6 August 1284: Genoa wins at Meloria.
1323: James II of Aragon invades Pisan Sardinia.
1324: Gallura leaves Pisan dominion.
1324: Sardinia is lost to Aragon.
1324: the Aragonese conquest of Pisan Sardinia is made.
13 February 1399: Pisa is sold to the Visconti.
1406: Florence annexes Pisa.

wars.name: Pisan wars with Genoa over Corsica
wars.outcome: Genoa won the battle of Meloria on 5-6 August 1284; Corsica 'fell to Genoa in 1284' (Corsica page); Pisa renounced any claim to it (Pisa page, which dates the end of its control to 1295).

wars.name: Pisan war on the Judicate of Cagliari
wars.outcome: Santa Igia fell in 1258 and the judicate 'was partitioned in three parts that were assigned to the Della Gherardesca family, Arborea and Gallura', Pisa keeping Castel di Castro.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Pisan Sardinia
wars.outcome: James II and Hugh II of Arborea occupied the Pisan lands of Cagliari and Gallura and the city of Sassari in 1323; the conquest of the island begins in 1324 and ends Pisa's Sardinian control ('Sardinia from 1207 to 1324').

wars.name: Florentine annexation of Pisa
wars.outcome: Pisa, a Visconti dominion since 1399, was annexed by Florence in 1406; Cliopatria ends the Republic in 1401.

wars.name: Balearic expedition
wars.outcome: 'Pisan merchants were among the initiators of the 1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition'; the infobox control span reads 'Balearics from 1115 to 1184'.

certainty.note: The contado's land frontier with Lucca, Florence and Volterra ('perennial struggle', no years or lines on the page) was never surveyed; the island coasts of Corsica and Sardinia are natural limits but Pisan control of both was dominion…
